title: Find Maximum Removals From Source String
summary: Given a string source of size n, a string pattern that is a subsequence of source, and a sorted integer array targetIndices containing distinct numbers in the range [0, n - 1], determine the maximum number of characters that can be removed from source such that pattern remains a subsequence of the modified source.
statement: Given a string source of size n, a string pattern that is a subsequence of source, and a sorted integer array targetIndices containing distinct numbers in the range [0, n - 1], determine the maximum number of characters that can be removed from source such that pattern remains a subsequence of the modified source. The indices in targetIndices must be used exactly once for removal, and the removal of a character does not change the indices of the other characters in source.
constraints: source length is at most 3,000; pattern is a guaranteed subsequence.
Only original positions in sorted target_indices may be removed, and original indices never shift.
Return the maximum removals that still leave pattern as a subsequence.
hints: Track how many pattern characters have been matched and the most removable eligible positions so far.
For each source character, either skip/remove it or use it to match the next pattern character.
Skipping gains one only at a target index; matching copies the previous state without that gain.
These are the only choices for every character, so DP maximization covers every feasible retained subsequence.
editorial: These are the only choices for every character, so DP maximization covers every feasible retained subsequence.

tests.explanation: Either index one or two can be removed, but not both, so the maximum is one.
Both indexed characters lie outside the required d and can be removed.
